scope: Three specifically requested original papers; bibliographic metadata verified against formal publisher DOI records. Protocol facts checked in publisher fulltext or explicitly identified institutional author postprint. No scores or target-label budgets inferred from title/abstract alone.

bibliography.title: Fusion Convolutional Neural Network for Cross-Subject EEG Motor Imagery Classification
bibliography.metadata_source: Crossref publisher-deposited metadata, corroborated by publisher fulltext or institutional author postprint

studies.task_and_cohort: PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery dataset; separate binary left/right executed-movement and imagined-movement subsets; 103 of 109 participants after excluding 38, 88, 89, 92, 100 and 104.
studies.evaluation_design: Published §2.5 randomly assigns 70% / 10% / 20% of 37,080 pooled labelled samples/windows to train / validation / test with fixed seed. This is not a documented participant-disjoint held-out-subject evaluation, despite the title. No cross-dataset transfer experiment is reported.
studies.target_label_and_calibration_boundary: Labels are used for the pooled training and validation samples. There is no designated unseen target cohort or zero-target-participant-label calibration budget in this protocol; therefore classify this budget as not applicable / not established, not as zero. Test labels are used for scoring.
studies.unlabelled_target_statistics: Paper reports notch60Hz and bandpass2–60Hz preprocessing and learned BatchNorm layers. No explicit target-domain distribution adaptation stage is described; no independently inspected code or normalization-statistics provenance audit was performed, so do not assert target-statistics exclusion.
studies.model_selection: Best validation-accuracy checkpoint retained/loaded (§2.5). The paper evaluates branch hyperparameter choices but does not provide a prospectively frozen participant-disjoint source-only selection and target-inference evidence chain.
studies.architecture_and_filters: Three separately parameterized EEGNet-style branches with temporal kernel lengths64/128/256 and differing filter counts; learned branch features are concatenated before classification. All branches receive the same bandpass-preprocessed input. This is multiscale/multibranch fusion, not fixed μ/β views sharing one backbone parameter set.
studies.metrics_and_unit: Ordinary classification accuracy (correct labels / total), precision, recall, F1 and runtime per sample. Original4-second trials are divided into eight nonoverlapping0.5-second windows, each with the trial label; no participant-level BA estimand in §2.5.
studies.limitations_for_current_paper: Do not quantitatively compare its headline ordinary sample/window accuracy with the current participant-level balanced-accuracy transfer estimates. Cite as architecture precedent while stating protocol non-equivalence. Pooled-window random splitting also gives no guarantee of trial-level or participant-level disjointness.

bibliography.title: Improving subject transfer in EEG classification with divergence estimation
bibliography.metadata_source: Crossref publisher-deposited metadata, corroborated by publisher fulltext or institutional author postprint

studies.fulltext_version_note: MERL TR2025-044 institutional cover is dated2April2025 and says JNE2025, but publisher-deposited DOI metadata and PubMed39591745 identify the formal article as JNE21(6):066031 (2024), online16December2024. Use formal2024 bibliography, not technical-report/preprint year. The institutional postprint abstract matches publisher-deposited formal abstract; direct publisher PDF returned an anti-bot challenge, so the VoR fulltext itself was not independently recovered.
studies.task_and_cohort: RSVP binary target/non-target stimulus classification, not motor imagery; just over1million trials,64participants with two sessions. Data recorded1000Hz and provided250Hz; non-target trials subsampled to10:1 relative to target trials.
studies.evaluation_design: Within-dataset zero-shot subject transfer. Main experiments use28training and4test participants for100epochs. Ten partially overlapping subject splits ×10random seeds; within each split subject sets are disjoint. No cross-dataset MI transfer experiment.
studies.target_label_and_calibration_boundary: §2.1 describes training on source participants and at test time receiving only X from unseen test participants to infer Y. No target-subject fitting is described in these zero-shot experiments. Test labels nevertheless support performance evaluation; optimal λ/peak comparisons are selected from test performance (§§3.2 and6.2.2). Thus zero-shot target fitting does not imply fully source-only selection of reported optimal configurations.
studies.unlabelled_target_statistics: Censoring penalties estimate dependence between source latent features and subject/session IDs, with optional task-label conditioning, using training batches. No explicit test-subject adaptation/distribution alignment stage is described. Preprocessing and empirical exclusion of all target-derived normalization statistics are not established by the inspected Methods; mark that narrower detail unverified.
studies.model_selection: Main fixed100epoch hyperparameter sweep; optimal-λ peak comparisons pooled across censor modes/projection choices. Appendix6.2 uses24training/4validation/4test participants, best validation-performance checkpoint, max30epochs. Appendix6.2.2 explicitly selects λ giving best mean test performance; distinguish this peak analysis from prospectively source-only frozen model selection.
studies.architecture_and_filters: 1D CNN encoder, MLP task classifier, optional MLP projector and auxiliary censor network. Density-ratio mutual-information or Wasserstein critic censoring with marginal/conditional/complementary modes. Not a fixed overlapping-filter-bank or shared μ/β branch architecture.
studies.metrics_and_unit: Balanced accuracy and test/train balanced-accuracy generalization ratio; variability across seeds/splits/hyperparameters. Quantitative results are not comparable to current MI cross-dataset cohorts/tasks.
studies.limitations_for_current_paper: Cite as general EEG zero-shot subject-transfer and selection-sensitivity precedent, explicitly RSVP rather than MI. Do not label its ideal-parameter results a source-only frozen selection benchmark. Do not cite2023 arXiv title Stabilizing Subject Transfer in EEG Classification with Divergence Estimation as the final formal title/year.
evidence_locators: Institutional postprint §2.1 (printedp4), §2.9 (pp10–11), §3.2 (p12), Appendix6.2/6.2.2 (pp19–20); formal metadata Crossref +PubMed39591745

bibliography.title: Overlapping filter bank convolutional neural network for multisubject multicategory motor imagery brain-computer interface
bibliography.metadata_source: Crossref publisher-deposited metadata, corroborated by publisher fulltext or institutional author postprint

studies.task_and_cohort: BCIIV2a/BNCI2014_001:9participants/four MIclasses; High-Gamma:14participants/four motor-execution/rest classes (not MI); OpenBMI:21selected of54participants/binary left-right MI after excluding33 designated MI-blind subjects.
studies.evaluation_design: Pooled multisubject within-dataset recognition. All9BNCI participants contribute training and test-session data; all14High-Gamma participants contribute earlier-run training and later-run testing. OpenBMI uses selected21participants and recordedtrain/test sets. No participant-disjoint unseen-target design or cross-dataset frozen transfer is described.
studies.target_label_and_calibration_boundary: Dataset participants contribute labelled training data; future test-session participants are represented in the training cohort. Therefore not zero-target-participant-label fitting. No distinct unseen target-participant calibration budget is defined; mark not applicable rather than zero.
studies.unlabelled_target_statistics: Exponential running channel standardization is applied to filtered EEG (Experimentalsetup,p8). This is input-dependent preprocessing, not evidence of a source-only fixed normalization-statistics contract. The paper does not document a separate target adaptation stage; exact training-versus-test running-statistics reset/fit provenance was not verified from execution.
studies.model_selection: BNCI/High-Gamma maximum500epochs; OpenBMI300epochs; average test accuracy/F1/AUC over final100epochs reported. Frequency-step sensitivity study selects4Hz as an empirical choice based on reported test results(Table4/Fig5,p13), not a prospectively source-only locked validation selection. No separate validation-fold checkpoint selection described in reviewed Experimentalsetup.
studies.architecture_and_filters: Multiple independent CNN models, one per overlapping bandpass-filtered view, trained separately with cross-entropy; output probabilities summed beforeargmax(Eqs2–4). Backbones shallow/deepConvNet,EEGNet,ATCNet. Table1 fixed low-cut examples0–8,0–12,…0–36Hz and4–12,4–16,…4–36Hz; sliding examples0–12,4–16,…24–36Hz. Explicitly separate models, not parameter-sharing μ/β backbone.
studies.metrics_and_unit: Ordinary accuracy(%),F1,AUC and test-accuracy variance averaged over the last100training epochs. No participant-level BA matched to current zero-calibration transfer estimand.
studies.limitations_for_current_paper: Relevant overlapping-filter-bank/ensemble precedent, not a direct unseen-subject or cross-dataset source-only comparator. Do not imply superiority or numerical equivalence across unequal class counts, tasks, cohort exclusions, metrics, split and epoch-selection rules. Formal2023 paper has7authors, includingJundongLi andHaiqinLiu; ResearchSquare preprints have different authorlists/name spelling and must not supply final citation metadata.
evidence_locators: PublisherPDF Table1/Eqs2–4(pp5–6); Experimentaldata(pp7–8); Experimentalsetup(p8); performancecomparison(p9); sensitivitystudy(Table4/Fig5,p13)

safe_synthesis: Multibranch fusion and overlapping-filter-bank ensembles are established EEG approaches, and dependence-censoring has been studied for zero-shot EEG subject transfer. The current study should therefore frame its contribution as a source-only model-selection audit with participant heterogeneity, frozen cross-dataset evaluation, retention of adverse/null results, and a reproducible evidence chain, not as the first multibranch representation or a new state-of-the-art domain-generalization algorithm. The three precedents do not provide a protocol-matched performance ranking: Roots uses a pooled-window random split; Luo uses same-cohort multisubject train/test sessions; Smedemark-Margulies studies RSVP with test-based optimal-λ peak analyses.
